Where it began

Mohammad Kaif was born in Allahabad, the city also known as Prayagraj, on 1 December 1980. He learned his cricket at Green Park in Kanpur, and the game ran in the family: his father, Mohammad Tarif Ansari, played for Railways and Uttar Pradesh, and his brother Mohammad Saif played for Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

He first made his name as a captain. In 2000 he led India to victory at the Under-19 World Cup, and the new National Cricket Academy in Bangalore took him in its very first group of players.

The player

His Test debut came against South Africa in Bangalore in March 2000, when he was 19. He came and went from the side for a few years, then returned against Australia in late 2004 with two fifties. In 2006 he top-scored with 91 against England at Nagpur, and that summer in the West Indies he made his one Test hundred, 148 not out.

In all he played 13 Tests between 2000 and 2006, scoring 625 runs at 32.89 with a hundred and three fifties, and holding 15 catches.

What made him special

Fielding was his gift. Patrolling the covers, he was quick to the ball and accurate with the throw, and batters thought twice before running to him. At the 2003 World Cup he held four catches against Sri Lanka in Johannesburg, the most by a fielder in one World Cup match.

With the bat he was a cool head in a chase, happy to turn the strike over and build a partnership. His most famous innings came in the 2002 NatWest Series final at Lord's, where his unbeaten 87 helped India chase down 326 and won him the man of the match award. India mostly used him in the middle order, though he tended to do his best work at number three, a place with plenty of fine players queuing for it in his day.

Away from the middle

He was part of the India side that shared the 2002 Champions Trophy with Sri Lanka, and he was in the squad that reached the 2003 World Cup final. He captained Uttar Pradesh and Central Zone, later played for Andhra and Chhattisgarh, and retired from all cricket in July 2018.

In the first IPL, in 2008, he played every match as Rajasthan Royals won the title. He went on to coach, as an assistant with Gujarat Lions in 2017 and Delhi Capitals in 2019 and 2020.

And finally

He bowled in Tests without taking a wicket. Given all the runs he saved in the covers, nobody in the India dressing room was going to complain.
